candidates.body:
Closes #47

The map camera was clamped to fixed heights (200 km to 40,000 km) whatever the map's size or view mode. Zoom limits are now computed per map.

## Changes

- **`computeCameraZoomLimits`** in `map-utils.ts` returns the limits for a map:
  - **Zoom in** stops where the basemap would pixelate: one image pixel per screen pixel across the map's larger dimension.
  - **Zoom out** stops where the whole map fills the view.
  - Each limit is loosened by a named constant: `ZOOM_IN_SLACK = 2` (2× over-zoom) and `ZOOM_OUT_SLACK = 1.5` (the map can shrink to about two thirds of the view).
- **Per view mode:** Cesium compares the limits to different things per mode: height above the surface in 3D and Columbus view, and the larger visible span in 2D. Each mode gets its own formula.
- **`Map.tsx`** recomputes the limits on creation, on resize (`ResizeObserver`), on view-mode switch (`morphComplete`) and on basemap change. The basemap's resolution is read from the imagery provider's tiling scheme, and the code waits for the provider to finish loading.
- **GIBS basemap config fix:** the `500m` tile matrix set serves 512 px tiles at levels 0–7. The provider declared 256 px tiles and `maximumLevel: 8`, and level 8 requests return HTTP 400. With the corrected config, the finest resolution is about 490 m per pixel.
- The fixed `MIN_ZOOM_DISTANCE` / `MAX_ZOOM_DISTANCE` constants are removed from `lib/gibs.js`.

## Example limits (3D)

| Map size | Zoom in | Zoom out |
|---|---|---|
| 578×322 px | 122 km | 24,868 km |
| 328×322 px | 69 km | 13,024 km |

## Testing

- **Unit:** 16 new tests for the zoom math cover all three modes, wide/tall/square maps, field of view and basemap resolution. `map-utils.ts` stays at 100% mutation score.
- **Manual browser check** (Chromium on an Apple M1 GPU, using a temporary patch that exposes the viewer):
  - The applied limits match the formula, and the camera stops at both limits in 3D, 2D and Columbus view.
  - The limits update when the map is resized.
  - Basemap tiles load at levels 0–7 with no failed requests and no WebGL errors.
  - In 2D, Cesium's own whole-world cap (about 40,075 km) applies before ours.
- **Gap:** there's no automated e2e test for the map, because checking the limits needs access to the Cesium viewer, which the app doesn't expose.
- **Pre-existing failure:** `Entities.spec.ts` fails on `develop` too (it looks for an `ACC1A` page the mocked view doesn't have).

candidates.body:
Closes #173

Products like OFFRED store field ids and values as key-value pairs, so a channel field's `enum_values` can run to tens of thousands of entries. Both channel dropdowns rendered every one of them as a Radix `Select` item, which made them unusable.

## Changes

- **`ChannelValueCombobox`**: a new searchable picker built on the same Stellar `Popover` + `Command` pattern as the Field picker. Filtering is done in the component (`shouldFilter={false}`) and at most 100 matches are rendered, with a "Showing 100 of N values. Type to narrow the list." note when more exist.
- **`filterChannelValues` / `sortChannelValues`** in `entity-editor-utils.ts`: matching ignores case and ranks values that start with the query ahead of values that merely contain it (typing `12` shows `12, 120, …` before `112, 312`). Values are sorted once in natural order, without mutating the product's `enum_values` (the old code re-sorted it in place on every render).
- Used in both places that picked channel values: `ProductSelector` (entity editor) and `ProductPreviewModal`.
- **Fix:** in the entity editor, a picked channel value didn't show on the trigger until the selection was complete (i.e. a version was also picked), because it was read from the committed `selectedProduct` prop instead of the draft state. This predates this PR.

The combobox is used for every channel, not only large ones; for short lists it behaves like a dropdown with a search box.

Free-text entry of a value missing from `enum_values` is **not** supported. If OFFRED's enumerated list can be incomplete, that's worth a follow-up.

## Testing

- Unit: 7 tests for the matching helpers and 7 component tests, including a 20,000-value set that renders only 100 options. All 289 unit tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Mutation: `entity-editor-utils.ts` stays at 100%.
- E2E: `ChannelValuePicker.spec.ts` mocks a product with a 20,000-value channel, then searches, picks a value and checks the trigger shows it.
- Live data (`mass-change-viz`, via the dev server, read-only): GRACE-FO GF1 OFFRED's `pcf_name` channel has **17,403 values**, far more than any other channel across the 145 products (the next largest is LHK1A/B `sensorname` at 91). In the Products page preview, the picker opened at once with 100 options and the "Showing 100 of 17403" note. Searching for `SDT50092.rn` narrowed it to that value, and the chart then loaded 33 points filtered on `pcf_name: SDT50092.rn`.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

candidates.body:
## Why

Stryker's vitest runner defaults to the `threads` pool (a worker thread per test file) while `vitest run` uses
`forks` (a process per file), so an import that cannot load in a second worker thread passes the gate and fails the
weekly Mutation job. template-next-seo went red that way on 2026-11-09: a native addon loaded through
`next-intl/plugin` failed with "Module did not self-register" before Stryker mutated anything
(Vadymk95/template-next-seo#142). No test here loads a native addon today, so this repo is green; the same default
would turn it red the day one arrives. Stryker 10.0 hid such failures (a file that fails to load counted as no
tests); 10.1.x, which runs here, reports them.

## What

- `stryker.config.json`: `vitest.pool: "forks"` (an option new in 10.1.0).
- `scripts/mutation-scope.test.mjs`: fails when the pool Stryker names differs from the one `vitest.config.ts` names
  (the vitest default `forks` when it names none), and when an `include` pattern starts with `**`, the form that
  would collect `.stryker-tmp`, the full copy a failed Stryker run leaves behind. Every `include` here starts at the
  repository root, and probe files under a stale sandbox were not collected, so no `exclude` is added.
- The Mutation workflow comment and a DECISIONS entry.

## How tested

- The new guards on the old config: the pool case fails (`stryker vitest.pool is "threads" but vitest run uses
  "forks"`); with a temporary `**/` include pattern the anchor case fails too; both pass on this change.
- `npx stryker run --dryRunOnly --concurrency 4`: the same number of tests ran under `threads` and `forks`, so no
  test file is dropped today.
- Lead mutations: `"pool": "forks"` -> `"threads"` and an include pattern turned into `**/src/...`, both caught.
- On the real runner (Mutation dispatched on this branch, run 42862542388): `Ran 243 tests`, score 59.72 against
  break 40 (last weekly 59.60). Cost: the run took 16 min 21 s against 11 min 9 s for the last weekly run, one
  sample each; the job is scheduled, so nobody waits on it.

## What changed

`vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` are held at `^4.1.11`. Dependabot ignores both at `>=5`. The hold is recorded in AGENTS.md Version holds and in DECISIONS.md with the measured numbers.

## Why

The weekly mutation job has been red on 2026-09-14, 09-21 and 09-28. Under vitest 5 the Stryker vitest runner 10.0.0 kills almost nothing: cold score about 9.6 against a break of 40, with fully covered files scoring 0. template-next-seo has held vitest 4.1 and stayed green.

The September reading that called vitest 5 a pass here came from a stale local `reports/stryker-incremental.json`. CI never has that file, so CI always runs cold.

## How it was verified

- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages, with its unit pass counts. The exit code was read without a pipe.
- [x] Covered by a test that fails when reverted. Cold `npm run test:mutation` (incremental report deleted first) was red before the hold and passes after it, with no threshold changed. template-1: 9.59 → 43.49. template-spa-pwa: 9.61 → 44.50. The unit suite and coverage pass unchanged on 4.1.11. An independent checker confirmed the versions, the log order against the lock file, and that the shared block is untouched.
- [ ] Visual check: no UI changed.

## Deliberately not touched

Stryker config and thresholds, jsdom 30, and the open Dependabot group PR.

## Risks

A vitest 5-only feature cannot be used until the hold is lifted. The lift trigger is in DECISIONS.md.

- **Probe:** stops its server group on every way out and the group a killed probe left (identity checked by start time and spawn arguments); `--signed-in` and `--theme` reach a protected route or a theme.
- **Tailwind:** scans the app folders only (`source(none)` plus `@source` lines), pinned by a build test.

## Why

`playwright install-deps` on the runner's apt mirror stalled 12 of 152 cross-browser steps (over 150 s or red) on
3 of 13 days between 2026-10-16 and 2026-11-10, across the three web templates. The three-try loop with a kill
between tries cannot outlast a mirror at about 57 kB/s: one master run went red after 9 minutes on all three tries.

## What

The same change as template-1 (Vadymk95/template-1#133); the two jobs are byte-identical to it.

- `cross-browser` runs in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<locked @playwright/test>-resolute` with `--user 1001`,

## What changed

- The commit hook no longer fails a commit whose staged files are all ones a linter ignores: the `lint-staged` oxlint command gets `--no-error-on-unmatched-pattern`, and the eslint command gets `--no-warn-ignored`.
- `gate-integrity.yml` reads the pull request's labels from the API when the job runs, instead of from the event payload, and its runs queue (`cancel-in-progress: false`) instead of cancelling each other. It gains `pull-requests: read`. `scripts/gate-tiers.json` and the README follow.
- The cross-browser job's `playwright install-deps` step gives each try 180 s (`timeout --kill-after=15s 180s`) and retries twice. A failed try kills what is left of apt-get and dpkg as root (`sudo pkill -KILL -x 'apt-get|dpkg'`) and runs `sudo dpkg --configure -a`, because Playwright runs apt-get through sudo and the timeout's signal never reaches it. A normal install takes 24 to 77 s (18 green runs), but a stalled apt on the runner held the job until its 20-minute timeout or a manual cancel four times in one afternoon.
- `scripts/lint-staged-coverage.test.mjs`: both describes take `{ timeout: 60_000 }`, as the same tests do in the other three templates. Its ESLint case starts ESLint twice and timed out at the default 5 s in the push gate under machine load (5,464 ms).

## Why

- oxlint exits 1 with "No files found to lint" when every file it is given matches its `ignorePatterns`. A commit of only `src/vite-env.d.ts` or `public/mockServiceWorker.js` therefore failed the hook. ESLint printed a "File ignored" warning for the service worker.
- A pull request opened with the `gate-change` label fires `opened` and `labeled` in the same second. One run was cancelled, and the cancelled one could be the run GitHub counted, so the merge stayed blocked with every check green until the cancelled run was re-run. That happened on three pull requests in a row. A re-run also replayed the labels its run started with, which the README had to warn about.

## How it was verified

- Red first: two cases in `scripts/lint-staged-coverage.test.mjs` failed before the `lint-staged` change (`Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)`) and pass after it. Each case first proves its files are really ignored: oxlint exits 1 with "No files found to lint" and ESLint warns, both without the new flag. Then the command exactly as configured must exit 0 with no warning.
- Two mutations, each caught: the oxlint flag removed (1 failed), the eslint flag removed (1 failed).
- `check-gate-integrity.mjs` is unchanged; on template-1 it gave the same verdict for the compact `gh --jq` label array and the pretty `toJSON` one, and an empty array failed it.
- Related suites: `check-gate-integrity*`, `docs-check*`, `gate-config-coverage` and `self-test-capture`, 1,240 tests, green; `docs:check` clean.
- Live proof on template-1 (#131, opened with the label): both `gate-integrity` runs, `opened` and `labeled`, completed with success and none was cancelled; before the change three pull requests in a row showed one success and one cancelled run.
- This pull request was opened with the label too, so its own `gate-integrity` runs repeat that proof.
- The retry loop without the kill line failed live on this pull request (run 42821920585): try 1 timed out at 180 s, tries 2 and 3 failed in a second with "Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend. It is held by process 2904 (apt-get)". The earlier stand-in test had no root grandchild, so it missed this.
- Seeded test on real apt and sudo: an Ubuntu 26.04.1 container (sudo 1.9.17p2), the loop run by a non-root user as on the runner, the cap shortened to 15 s, and a first try that downloads through a proxy that never answers. The previous loop reproduced the lock failure (exit 1, apt-get still running afterwards); this loop installed on try 2 and exited 0; with every try stalled it made three real tries and exited 1 after 46 s, with no apt-get left. The loop under test was extracted from the committed `ci.yml`; the step block is byte-identical in the three web templates, and `docs:check` is clean.

- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages (`verify:push`; silence is a failure). Exit code read without a pipe: 0. 101 test files, 2,378 tests passed.
- [x] New behaviour is covered by a test that FAILS when the change is reverted (the two cases and the two mutations above; the workflow change by the live run on this pull request).
- [ ] Visual check at 390 / 768 / 1440 in both themes. Not applicable: no UI changed.

## Deliberately not touched

- `scripts/check-gate-integrity.mjs`: its `--labels` input stays a JSON array.

## Risks

- The job now needs `pull-requests: read` to read the labels. A fork's pull request gets a read-only token, which is enough.
- With runs queued instead of cancelled, a burst of label changes runs the job once per event. The job takes about 10 seconds.

## What changed

- The production-mode e2e run (gate and CI) now stops after 10 failures (`maxFailures`). Each Playwright config writes to its own `outputDir`.
- The shared harness block now says what to do after a red push: fix, rebuild if needed, re-run only the failed tests, push again.
- Dependency floors were raised past new high advisories that made `audit:gate` refuse every push. The details are in the second commit and `DECISIONS.md`.

## Why

A sibling product forked from these templates measured 30 days of its push gate:
- 22 of 60 pushes were red;
- red pushes took 35% of all push minutes;
- a red push ran up to 21 min, against ~5 for a green one.

The cause was no failure cap outside CI: every failing test waited out its own timeout. With one shared invariant broken (630 tests), the run took 7.5 min uncapped and 21 s with a cap of 10.

A shared default `test-results` folder let the next suite in the chain overwrite the `.last-run.json` that `--last-failed` reads.

## How it was verified

- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages (`verify:push`, phase 0) with its unit pass counts. The exit code was read without a pipe.
- [x] New behaviour is covered by a test that FAILS when the change is reverted. `scripts/check-playwright-gate-config.test.mjs` was red before the config change and green after. Mutation-checked: drop the cap and only the cap cases go red; make the two folders equal and only the folder case goes red.
- [ ] Visual check: no UI changed.
- `--last-failed` mechanics were proved on template-1. The record lands in the config's own folder, and a re-run selects exactly the failed test.
- Playwright 1.63 writes never-run tests into the record too (`lib/runner/index.js`: `!t.ok() || didNotRun(t)`). That is why the rule names spec files after a capped stop.
- `npm audit --audit-level=high` and `audit:gate`: exit 0 after the floor change.

## Deliberately not touched

Retries, workers, timeouts and specs are unchanged, and what a green push runs is unchanged. The open Dependabot and release PRs are not part of this.

## Risks

None that I can see for green runs. A red run now reports at most 10 failures instead of all of them, which is the intended trade.

## What changed

- An effect that starts a browser subscription and never releases it now fails lint. Every `no-leaked-*` rule of `eslint-plugin-react-web-api` is an error over the files the React rules cover: event listener, fetch, IntersectionObserver, interval, ResizeObserver and timeout. The plugin is pinned exactly at 5.28.8, and the rules are named one by one rather than taken from a preset. This is the template-1 pilot (#128) ported as it landed there.
- The commit hook now formats every file the push gate checks for format. The `lint-staged` code glob adds `.mjs` and `.cjs`; the prettier-only glob adds `.css` and `.html`.

## Why

- A listener, timer, observer or request started in an effect with no cleanup keeps running after the component unmounts. Types, unit tests and the other lint rules all pass on it.
- `format:check` runs `prettier --check .`, which reads every tracked file prettier can parse, while the hook formatted only `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `json`, `md`, `yml` and `yaml`. A misformatted `.mjs` script passed the commit and failed the push (seen in template-1 on 2026-11-07).

## How it was verified

- Leak lint, red first: the new guard cases in `scripts/lint-guards.test.mjs` failed before the plugin was configured (19 failed of 53) and pass after it (53 of 53).

Before the glob change it listed 76 files (74 `.mjs`, `index.html`, `src/index.css`); after it, 2 of 2 pass.

- `npx eslint . --no-cache --max-warnings 0` on the tree: 233 files, 0 hits of the new rules, so 0 false positives.
- Derived state: a value an effect rebuilds from other values is already reported by `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`; a guard case pins that, so no second effect plugin was added.
- Live run of the hook: a misformatted scratch `.mjs`, staged alone, ran no task before the glob change and came out formatted after it.
- Supply chain: `npm audit signatures` verified 398 attestations; `lock:age` and `audit:gate` pass. The lockfile diff only adds packages: the plugin, five `@eslint-react/*` packages and `ts-pattern`.

## What changed

- **Dependency audit:** `audit:gate` judges each advisory by its own rating, not by the package it was reached through. A low advisory behind a high-rated package no longer blocks, and a critical one behind a low-rated package does. One advisory reached through two packages is listed once, at the higher rating. An allowance for an advisory that no longer blocks is not stale, but it still goes red on its date, so such rows are removed.
- **Pre-commit sibling check:** a test file marked with `git add -N` no longer counts as a sibling. It sits in the index with no content and the commit leaves it out. A committed test that was dropped from the index and re-marked with `git add -N` does not count either, because the commit deletes it. What the commit carries is read as the HEAD tree plus the staged additions minus the staged deletions.
- **Docs check:** a suite in `gate-tiers.json` without a usable `dir`, `match`, `count` or `max` is reported instead of passing for ever; `docs/` is read as a doc folder; `file.ext:12:5` counts as a line pointer like `file.ext:12`.
- **Dependency holds:** `check-version-holds` takes a URL or the path of an existing file as evidence, never a path with a line number.
- **Gate integrity:** `npm run gate:integrity` finds its own base (`origin/master`, else `origin/main`), exits 2 when neither exists, and uses an explicit `--base` as given. A test pins `--no-renames` in the suppression scan.
- **Dependencies:** `follow-redirects` 1.16.1 to 1.16.2 in the lockfile (GHSA-mrwp-f3q8-3g9p, high, published 2026-10-30). The audit gate, the first stage of the push gate, was red on every push until then; the package is transitive, so only `package-lock.json` changes.
- **Size budgets:** every entry of `.size-limit.json` must carry a byte `limit` and `brotli: true` (size-limit skips an entry with no limit).
- **E2E:** `playwright.dev.config.ts` caps failures at 10 on CI like `playwright.config.ts`; the pin sits in `e2e/support/playwright-config.test.ts`.
- **Agent files:** the Ports rule says what happens when a pinned port is busy; a re-run writes to its own numbered log and the hand-back quotes the first red; on an agent-written change the reviewer mutates the fix in a disposable linked worktree; the logic step is a written plan with one adversarial pass instead of a named MCP server.

## Why

Each of these let a check pass, or fail, for the wrong reason: an advisory took the rating of whatever package it came through; an intent-to-add test counted as a sibling although the commit leaves it out; a suite ceiling that was absent, zero or a string compared false both ways and was never judged; a hold could cite a line that moves with every edit; `gate:integrity` failed where the default branch is `main`; the dev-smoke run waited out every failing test's timeout because only the production-server config capped failures.

## How it was verified

- Every new check has a spec that fails when the change is reverted. Red first where the old code could fail it: audit rating 5 cases, docs check 24, dependency holds 3, gate integrity 7; the cases that pin behaviour the old code already had (`--no-renames`, the size budget) were proven by mutation instead.
- Mutations of the new checks, run by hand in a disposable copy: 5 of 5 (sibling check, dev-smoke cap) and the 11 shared-script mutations run in template-1 (the scripts are byte copies) were caught by the named specs.
- The shared gate files and the `AGENTS.md` shared block are byte copies across the four templates (`check-shared-harness.sh` prints identical; `cmp` over the shared set).
- The pre-push gate (scaffold phase) ran all three stages in order and passed: `audit:gate`, `lock:age`, and `verify:scaffold` (docs check "no mechanical drift", format check, type check, oxlint and ESLint with zero warnings, 100 test files and 2352 tests with the coverage check).
- The sibling cases run against real temporary git repositories; locally that is git 2.50.1, and CI runs the same cases on the runner's git.

## Deliberately not touched

- Prose pointers in docs, the `examples/` folder in the docs check, and stale rows in `lock-age-allowlist.json` (reported, not changed here).

## Risks

- `docs:check` is stricter: a fork that copies the gate files may get new findings in its own `gate-tiers.json` suites or `docs/` folder, each naming the field or the file.
- An advisory whose own rating is below high no longer blocks even when its package is rated high; an advisory with no rating of its own falls back to the package rating.
- Labelled `gate-change`: the PR touches gate files.

## What changed

`trace:report` ends with a push ledger: the last 20 pushes, one row each with the start time, the verdict (`pass`, `red (exit N)` or `unknown`), the failed step, the duration and the commit (7 characters). A push is a row whose label the push moment of `scripts/gate-tiers.json` expects, so a hand-run gate row stays out. A column an older row does not have shows `-`. The ledger prints under a clean report and under one with findings.

`docs-check` gains a guard for the hand-kept moments map. Every label that a `package.json` script or a hook file passes to `gate-trace.mjs` must be on some moment's `expected` or `forbidden` list; otherwise it reports `scripts/gate-tiers.json: no moment lists "<label>", traced by <where>` and says which list to add it to. Comment lines are skipped and env prefixes are allowed. The guard is skipped, and left out of the summary line, when `gate-tiers.json` has no `moments`; otherwise the summary line names `moment labels`.

The shared harness block re-wraps its Prohibitions paragraph (one line of about 150 characters becomes three; same words), and the `trace:report` row of the command table now ends `, then the last 20 pushes`.

## Why

- Whether the last pushes went red, and at which step, took reading raw log rows; the ledger prints it at the end of the report.
- `moments` is a map kept by hand. A script renamed in `package.json` dropped out of `trace:report` without a word, because no moment listed the new label.

## How it was verified

- Red before, green after: with the slice's new tests in place and the old source, `Tests  18 failed | 788 passed (806)`, 9 of them this pull request's (3 ledger tests, 6 guard tests); with the new source `Tests  806 passed (806)`.
- Mutations, each file restored after the run (`mut.py`): the guard never reports (`.filter(() => false)`), caught by `names a traced label no moment lists, and the script that traces it` and 3 more; the ledger takes every row, not only push rows, caught by 2 ledger tests.

## What changed

The gate's Node scripts keep a child's whole output. One capture limit, `OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES` (256 MiB) in the new `scripts/child-output.mjs`, is set on every capture whose output can grow, and a child that passes it gets one line naming the limit and where to raise it (`ENOBUFS`). `check-coverage` sets `process.exitCode` and returns instead of calling `process.exit()` after it echoes a run, and `audit-gate` says when the audit document outgrew the limit instead of the bare "could not be completed". A new harness self-test, `scripts/output-limits.test.mjs`, fails on a capture without `maxBuffer` and on a file that echoes a child's output and calls `process.exit(`.

`npm run lint` drops `--cache`. A push with `GATE_PHASE=full` or `1` now prints that Prettier still reads `.prettiercache`, and the run that skips nothing.

This branch sits on #134, which empties the audit allowlist (GitHub withdrew the picomatch advisory, so every push was red). Merge that one first; its commit then drops out of this squash.

## Why

- A sync capture stops at `maxBuffer`, 1 MiB by default and shared by stdout and stderr. Past it the child is killed and the gate printed no reason: on Node 24.10, 600 KiB to each stream gives `error=ENOBUFS status=null signal=SIGTERM`.
- `process.exit()` right after a large write to a pipe keeps only the first 64 KiB, because pipes are asynchronous on POSIX (Node docs, "A note on process I/O"). Measured: `node -e "process.stdout.write('z'.repeat(1048576)); process.exit(0)" | wc -c` prints 65536; with `process.exitCode = 0` it prints 1048576. A red coverage run lost its tail, the part that names the failure.
- The push lint is type-aware, and typescript-eslint says `--cache` "will only work reliably for untyped rules -- and even then, not always" (https://typescript-eslint.io/troubleshooting/faqs/eslint/), so a cached verdict can be stale. Cost here, medians of three runs with one file changed: 4.0 s cached vs 11.6 s uncached, +7.6 s per push.
- The `GATE_PHASE=full` text said it "forces the full chain" while lint and Prettier still read their caches.

## How it was verified

- Red before the fix, with the new tests in place: `vitest run scripts/child-output.test.mjs scripts/verify-push.test.mjs` with `check-coverage`, `audit-gate` and `verify-push` at master: exit 1, `Tests 6 failed | 27 passed (33)` (the three large-output cases and the three banner cases).
- Green after: `child-output`, `output-limits`, `verify-push`, `check-coverage` and `audit-gate`: exit 0, `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 83 passed (83)`. Harness suite: the push below ran the whole unit suite in the main checkout, harness self-tests included.
- Mutations with each file restored after the run: `process.exit(result.status ?? 1)` back in `check-coverage.mjs`: caught; `maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024` in `check-coverage.mjs`: caught. `verify-push.mjs` and its test are byte-identical to template-1's, where dropping `'1'` from the override check was caught.
- Scan sabotage: `maxBuffer` removed from the `git` call in `lint-changed.mjs` gives `scripts/lint-changed.mjs:32 execFileSync() sets no maxBuffer`; `process.exit(1)` put back after the echo gives `scripts/check-coverage.mjs:90 writes a child's output and the file calls process.exit(`.
- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages (`verify:push`; silence is a failure), exit code read without a pipe: phase 0, exit 0 in 61 s; `Test Files 110 passed (110)`, `Tests 2639 passed (2639)`
- [x] New behaviour is covered by a test that FAILS when the change is reverted: the mutations above
- [ ] Visual check at 390 / 768 / 1440 in both themes, if any UI changed: n/a, no UI

## Deliberately not touched

- ESLint keeps its cache where it is a desk tool, not a verdict: `npm run fix`, lint-staged at commit, `lint-changed.mjs` in the iterate loop.
- Prettier keeps `.prettiercache` on `format:check`; the banner names it.
- Captures that already set `maxBuffer`, and every `stdio: 'inherit'` call.
- No verdict cache for the push: nothing here has a landing step whose green it could reuse, and it would save about 2 s of a 34 s push.

## Risks

- The scan reads text. A capture through an alias, a namespace import (`import * as cp`) or a default argument (`run = spawnSync`, fixed by hand in `server-group.mjs`) passes it unseen.
- The overflow line was not run end to end (that needs 256 MiB of output); its wiring was read and its text is unit-tested.
- The 64 KiB cut was measured on macOS only; Node's docs say POSIX pipes are asynchronous, so Linux CI should behave the same.

## What changed

The push runs its steps through one runner. `scripts/bench-verify.mjs` gains `expandSteps`, which returns a gate script's leaf steps in run order: `npm run` hops and the tracer wrapper are followed, every argument is kept, a segment npm hands to its shell runs through `sh -c`, and a cycle, a missing script or a `pre`/`post` script throws. It also gains `runSteps`, which inherits the output, prints one line before each step, stops at the first red and ends with one verdict line: `✖ <target>: step <label> failed (exit <code>) after <s> s; <k> later steps not run` or `✓ <target>: <n> steps passed in <s> s`. `verify-push.mjs` runs its target through `runScript` instead of `npm run <target>`, with the same environment. `npm run bench:verify -- --run <script>` runs any script the same way. The runner joins the `permissions.ask` list of gate scripts in `.claude/settings.json`.

Lines that ask a person to act start with `ACT`: the budget drift (`ACT budget: ...`) and the stale audit allowance. The stale line now says how to check whether an advisory was withdrawn (`gh api /advisories/<id>`, `withdrawn_at`) and what to do.

Coverage prints its four totals in the terminal (`text-summary`) instead of a row per file. A missed threshold is still named, and the per-file table is one flag away (`VERIFICATION.md`).

The shared harness block adds two rules. Every test command an agent runs names a worker cap, and a lane starts nothing heavy while the 1-minute load average is at or above the core count. A line that starts with `ACT` asks a person to act. `LANE.md` adds two more. A brief names that cap and that check. A lane prints a command's exit code, the log's first line and its last 40 lines, and names the log path.

## Why

- A red push printed npm's error for the whole `&&` chain and never said which step failed. A step list of its own (`bench:verify` had one) drops arguments such as `--range` and drifts from the gate.
- A line that needs a person read like any other line. On 2026-11-18 GitHub withdrew an advisory, and every push of the four templates went red on a bare `Stale allowlist entry` line until someone looked the advisory up.
- The `text` reporter printed a row per file into every coverage log, and nothing reads that table (`check-coverage.mjs` reads only the dropout lines). On a one-file run: a run of one test file printed 893 B with the totals; the push log lost its 18 per-file rows (7,142 B before, 3,831 B now).
- A lane that printed only a tail lost the first line of a run, the one that says what it selected. A command piped into `tail` also hid its exit code.

## How it was verified

- Red before, green after, with the new tests in place: with the new tests in place and the old source, `Tests 14 failed | 823 passed (837)`; with the new source, `Tests 902 passed (902)` (the implementer's runs).
- Mutations, each file restored after the run (`mut.py`): the parser drops a step's extra arguments again, caught by `bench-verify.test.mjs`; the reporter back to `text`, caught by `vitest-config.test.mjs`.
- With `text-summary`, a failed threshold is still named: a one-file run printed `ERROR: Coverage for lines (0.43%) does not meet global threshold (65%)` and the same line for functions, statements and branches, exit 1.
- This push ran the same leaf commands in the same order as the last push before the change: 12 of 12 steps equal the leaf commands of `verify:scaffold:push` expanded from `package.json`, and the last push before the change printed npm's script headers in that same run order (9 of 9).
- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages, exit code read without a pipe: `✓ verify:scaffold:push: 12 steps passed in 53.4 s` in phase 0 (`Tests 2653 passed (2653)`), exit 0
- [x] New behaviour is covered by a test that FAILS when the change is reverted: the mutations above
- [ ] Visual check at 390 / 768 / 1440 in both themes, if any UI changed: n/a, no UI

## Deliberately not touched

- These go to the next pull request, so this one stays inside its ~400-line budget:
  - the trace columns for the commit and the failed step;
  - the push ledger in `trace:report`;
  - the guard for the hand-kept moments map.

## Risks

- The push printed `ACT budget: ...` (4.79x of this machine's calibrated baseline). The same drift was printed before this change without the prefix; what grew is not part of this pull request.

## What changed

## What changed

- The cross-browser job's Playwright browser cache key now carries the runner's Ubuntu release (`ID` and `VERSION_ID` from `/etc/os-release`, for example `ubuntu-26.04`). A new `Read runner distro` step reads it and hands it to the cache step as a step output. `env.ImageOS` is not used: the `env` context of an expression does not carry variables the runner sets itself.
- `scripts/gate-tiers.json` lists the new step's two shell lines in `ci.allowedRunSteps`, each with a reason. `docs:check` refuses any `run:` line in `ci.yml` that is neither inside `verify` nor listed there.

## Why

`ubuntu-latest` now resolves to Ubuntu 26.04 (runner image 20261101). The old key held only the OS family and the lockfile hash, so a WebKit saved on Ubuntu 24.04 was restored on 26.04 and could not start (`libicudata.so.74` missing). The failure was seen on template-next-seo's #132; this repo has the same job and the same key. A new Ubuntu release now starts a fresh cache instead of restoring one the new release cannot run.

## How it was verified

- `docs:check` is the test for the two allow entries; with them it prints "no mechanical drift". The same check refused the same two lines in template-next-seo before the entries existed.
- Two mutations of the entries in a disposable worktree: the first entry's text changed by one letter, and the second entry without `${VERSION_ID}`. Both made `docs:check` exit 1 (2 of 2 caught).
- The pre-push gate ran 3 of 3 stages in order and passed (`pr-loop.sh gate-check` on the captured push log: `GATE PASSED`).
- CI on this PR, cross-browser job on Ubuntu 26.04: the `Read runner distro` step fed the cache key `playwright-xbrowser-Linux-ubuntu-26.04-<lockfile hash>`. The run logged `Cache not found for input keys: playwright-xbrowser-Linux-ubuntu-26.04-...` (the old key is no longer matched), saved the new cache and passed. A restore under the new key was exercised by a re-run on template-next-seo's PR (`Cache hit`, `Cache restored`, specs passed); it was not repeated here.

## Deliberately not touched

- The `ubuntu-latest` label, the other CI jobs, the `verify` chain and the lockfile.

## Risks

- The first CI run after the merge downloads the browsers again, because the key changed.
- Labelled `gate-change`: the PR touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `scripts/gate-tiers.json`.

## Why

Dependabot opens the version updates and a person merges each of them by hand after the checks. The patch and minor ones need no decision once the required checks are green, so the hand merge is pure upkeep. Majors stay with a person.

## What changed

- A workflow, `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`, runs on a pull request opened by `dependabot[bot]` and asks GitHub to merge it (squash) once the required checks pass. It never merges anything itself and bypasses no rule.
- The logic lives in `scripts/dependabot-auto-merge.sh`, checked out from the **base** branch (sparse checkout of that one file), so the code that runs with a write token never comes from the pull request.
- It asks only when all of these hold: the update is a patch or a minor one; the repository allows auto-merge; the base branch has at least one required status check (ruleset or classic protection). Without a required check GitHub would merge at once, so the script enables nothing and says why.
- A major update, or metadata that could not be read, gets no request. A request the workflow made earlier is switched off in that case; a request a person made is left in place and the line names the person.
- One new `ci.allowedRunSteps` entry in `scripts/gate-tiers.json` (`bash scripts/dependabot-auto-merge.sh`). The 7-day cooldown in `dependabot.yml` is unchanged.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New tests red before the code | `scripts/dependabot-auto-merge.test.mjs`, the first red output kept |
| The new test file | 43 passed, 0 failed (lead's re-run) |
| Lead mutations | 3 of 3 caught: the required-check guard never fires (3 tests fail); a person's request is switched off (1 fails); the script is checked out from the head ref (1 fails) |
| Required checks, read live on this repository | ruleset for `master`: 7; classic protection: 0; the script's filter prints 7 |
| GitHub's answer on an already green pull request, live | `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` on a pull request with all checks green answered `UNPROCESSABLE: Pull request is in clean status`, exit 1, nothing merged; the script prints that line with what to do next |
| `zizmor` 1.30.1, offline, all workflows | no findings |
| Push gate on this branch | 105 test files, 2,499 tests passed |

Still owed, after the merge (the workflow has to exist on the default branch first): `@dependabot rebase` on one patch-or-minor pull request (must get the request and merge after the 7 checks, `auto_merge.enabled_by.login` must be `github-actions[bot]`) and on one major (must get none).

## Known limits

- A merge made on a request of the workflow token starts no workflow run on the default branch. The required checks ran on the pull request; the next ordinary push runs the default-branch jobs.
- A pull request that is already green when the job runs is refused by GitHub (see the table); the job goes red with the instruction to comment `@dependabot rebase` or merge by hand.

## Weight

- Script code +73 lines (69 shell, 4 config), script tests +548, workflow +67, docs +6.
- A fork's push gains 1 test file and 43 test cases: this change adds harness tests to every push.
- Files an ordinary feature must touch: unchanged.
- Paid by: 129 Dependabot pull requests since 2026-08-01, each merged by hand.

## Review notes

Gate files changed (`.github/workflows/**`, `scripts/**`, `scripts/gate-tiers.json`), so the `gate-integrity` check needs the `gate-change` label.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Given** a clone where `core.hooksPath` is `.husky/_` and that folder holds no hook file, **when** `node scripts/check-hooks.mjs` runs, **then** it exits 1, names the hooks git would skip and prints `npm run prepare`.
- **Given** a hook file that lost its exec bit, **when** the check runs, **then** it exits 1 and prints a `chmod +x` remedy, never `npm run prepare` (husky leaves the mode of an existing file alone).
- **Given** a clone after `npm run prepare`, **when** the check runs, **then** it exits 0 and prints nothing.

## What changed

`scripts/check-hooks.mjs` now reads the hook file of every hook that has a body under `.husky/`: the file must exist in the folder git runs hooks from and pass the exec test git applies. A missing file and a file without the exec bit are refused by name, each with the remedy that repairs it. The new check runs before the `core.hooksPath` comparison, so a clone with neither the path nor the files gets one remedy instead of two rounds.

The spec (`scripts/check-hooks.test.mjs`) now builds husky's real layout in a throwaway repository (bodies under `.husky/` at mode 644, hook files at 755, husky's helper files) and gains 9 cases at run time (7 `it(` calls, one of them a loop over the three hooks): each hook file missing in turn, helper files only, a hook file without the exec bit, both states in one run, every hook name the installed husky wires (taken from a real installer run and compared as exact lists), a file under `.husky/` that is not a hook name needs no hook file, and path unset plus files missing gives one remedy. The 9 older cases keep their assertions and run on the same real layout; the CI case now has bodies and no hook file.

## Why

The check passed whenever the folder existed and the path pointed at it; it never read a file inside. Measured on 2026-11-13 in a throwaway repository: with the path right and the folder holding husky's helper files only, the check exited 0 and a real commit ran no hook. Nothing is broken in this repository today (its hooks are installed); this repairs the guard that would not have seen the day they go missing.

## How it was verified

| Proof | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Three-layout fixture, layout "path right, no hook file" | check exit 0, no hook ran on a commit | check exit 1, names the three hooks, prints `npm run prepare` |
| The fixture's other two layouts (husky 8 layout, husky 9 layout) | exit 1, exit 0 | exit 1, exit 0 |
| The new spec against the old script | 8 failed, 10 passed (18 cases) | 18 passed (18 cases) |
| Mutations of the fix, one at a time in a disposable worktree | n/a | 2 of 2 caught here (failed cases in the mutated run): one name dropped from the husky list, 1; the not-executable refusal printed always, 4. The script and the spec are byte copies of template-1's, where 6 of 6 were caught |
| The new script in this repository's main checkout (husky's real layout) | n/a | exit 0, no output |
| The push gate, run from the main checkout | n/a | `verify:push` at phase 0 with all harness self-tests (a harness path changed): `Test Files 108 passed (108)`, `Tests 2626 passed (2626)`, push exit 0 |

- [x] The push gate ran and printed its stages (`verify:push`; silence is a failure) — exit code read without a pipe
- [x] New behaviour is covered by a test that FAILS when the change is reverted
- [ ] Visual check at 390 / 768 / 1440 in both themes, if any UI changed — no UI changed

Weight: script code +60 / -2; script tests +144 / -27; docs +2 / -1. Test files added: 0; test cases added: 7 (static count; 9 at run time). Over the round's own budget of 150 added script lines: 204 (60 code, 144 tests); no case was cut to fit.

`gate-integrity` is red by design until a reviewer adds the `gate-change` label: the change touches gate files (`scripts/check-hooks.mjs`, `scripts/check-hooks.test.mjs`).

## Deliberately not touched

- The other gate scripts and the convergence of the template copies: `scripts/check-hooks.mjs` stays one blob across the four templates, nothing else moves.
- `HUSKY=0` in a developer's environment makes husky's own runner skip every hook body while this check stays green (CI sets it on purpose). Seen, not part of this change.
- No new `DECISIONS.md` entry: the README paragraph and the script header carry the new fact.

## Risks

- On Windows `fs.constants.X_OK` behaves like an existence test (Node docs, not checked here), so the exec-bit refusal would not fire there and the spec's exec-bit case would fail. CI runs on Linux.
- The list of hook names in the script is a copy of the installed husky's list; a spec case runs the real installer and fails when the two differ, so a husky upgrade that wires a new hook name turns that case red until the list is read again.

## What

The gate chain (which checks run, in which order, per moment and phase) now has one readable home, and the docs
stop retelling it. `package.json` `scripts` stays the only definition of what runs: no chain changed.

- **One checked view**: `scripts/gate-tiers.json` shows the chain of each multi-step gate script
  (`checks.<name>.chain`, `verify:scaffold:push` included). docs-check derives each chain from `package.json` and
  fails when the view differs.
- **Pointers, not retellings**: README, AGENTS.md, `.cursor/brain`, `.cursor/rules`, `.cursor/docs`, the CI step
  names and the `.husky/pre-push` comments name a script and what it is for, and point at `scripts/gate-tiers.json`
  for its stages. The prose inside `gate-tiers.json` states purpose only.
- **A guard so retellings do not come back**: docs-check flags a line that composes the gate (two parts of one gate
  script close together, or a script and one of its own parts), whatever the count. The names come from the repo
  (`package.json` chains, `checks`, `docs.stageWords`), not from a list of spellings. The rule, its windows, the
  measured catch and noise, and what it does not catch: `.cursor/brain/DECISIONS.md` § "The gate chain has one
  readable home".
- **`npm run gate:integrity`** in template-spa-pwa, template-next-seo and template-rn, as in template-1.
- **`.claude/settings.json`**: an agent is asked before it edits a gate script, its data or config, or an

## Why

Every late review round of the previous harness batch found a chain retold out of step with `package.json`: a stale
chain in AGENTS.md, and `verify:ci` written in reverse in two templates. Nothing stopped a new retelling.

## How tested

Three rounds of implementer plus independent verifier, each guard red first.

- Catch on the pre-change docs (places that retold a chain, caught by the shipped rule): template-1 32 of 32,

- docs-check suite 643 tests, the same cases in vitest (three web templates) and node:test (template-rn), green.

Not covered, by design (listed in the DECISIONS entry): compositions spread over sentences, lines or past the word
windows; two bare words with no mark; script comments, code, issue templates and app copy; a one-name statement in a
`gate-tiers.json` description. Also not read: a one-name alias statement in the docs (`verify` named as the alias of
`verify:enterprise`); an alias is a one-step script, so it has no parts to compose. In template-next-seo and

## What changed

- `app.config.ts`, which is not a gate file, holds the manifest identity (`name`, `short_name`, `description`, `lang`, `theme_color`, `background_color`) and the web-font list; `vite.config.ts` spreads `manifestIdentity` into the manifest and passes the font list to `vite-plugin-webfont-dl`. `tsconfig.node.json` includes the new module.
- `e2e/support/preview-mode.ts` exports `isPreviewRun(env)`; `playwright.config.ts`, `e2e/sw-lifecycle.spec.ts` and `e2e/security-headers.spec.ts` all ask it whether the preview build runs.
- `src/lib/zod.ts` sets `z.config({ jitless: true })` and re-exports `z`; every module under `src` imports `z` from `@/lib/zod`. ESLint's `no-restricted-imports` bans `zod` and `zod/**` everywhere else under `src`, tests and type-only imports included. That block restates the FC ban and the parent-relative group, because flat config replaces a rule's options instead of merging them. `vite.config.ts` exempts that one module from `treeshake.moduleSideEffects: false`, so the production bundle keeps the `jitless` call.
- The default button variant hovers to a new `--primary-hover` token instead of `primary/90`.
- `.cursor/rules/api.mdc` cites no sample file.
- Every self-test that starts a child process captures its output; `scripts/self-test-capture.test.mjs` fails on a child started without captured output.
- README: where CodeQL works and what a private fork needs, with both GitHub docs links. The brain docs and `SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md` follow.

## Why

- Every fork must change the manifest's name, description and colours ("Replace this description before shipping"), and they sat in `vite.config.ts`, a gate file. Each fork's first PR failed `gate-integrity` until a human added the label, and the label stopped meaning "the gate changed".
- `sw-lifecycle.spec.ts` skipped unless `baseURL` contained `:4173`, while `PORT` moves the server: a fork ran its e2e with `PORT=5183` and the three service-worker specs never ran.
- A fork built a schema at load time in a new module that loaded before `src/env.ts`; zod's default probed `new Function` and the shipped CSP blocked it. Import order was the only protection. With `moduleSideEffects: false` the bundler would also drop the body of a module that only re-exports `z`, `jitless` call included, which a unit test cannot see.
- The primary button's text on hover was 4.13:1 (light) and 4.10:1 (dark), under the 4.5:1 AA needs for 14 px text.
- Deleting the sample pages left `.cursor/rules/api.mdc` citing `src/pages/HomePage/useHomePage.ts`; docs-check flagged it, and the fork had to edit a gate file.
- Test runs printed lines like "Git hooks are not installed (lifecycle scripts are disabled by .npmrc)." from children with inherited output, which read like real failures.
- In a private repository without code scanning the CodeQL job fails ("Code scanning is not enabled for this repository") while the ruleset requires its check.

## How tested

- Red first, each new test against the unfixed code: `scripts/app-identity.test.mjs`, `scripts/preview-only-specs.test.mjs`, `e2e/support/preview-mode.test.ts`, `scripts/lint-guards.test.mjs`, `scripts/zod-config-bundle.test.mjs`, `src/lib/zod.test.ts`, `scripts/button-contrast.test.mjs`, `scripts/self-test-capture.test.mjs`.
- Mutation in a scratch copy, 12 of 12 went red: the manifest `name` back in `vite.config.ts`; the service-worker spec back to the port check; `isPreviewRun` reading the port; from the zod lint block, the `zod` path, the `zod/**` pattern, the `zod.ts` exemption, the FC ban or the parent-relative group dropped; `moduleSideEffects: false` for every module; the hover back to `primary/90`; the `jitless` call removed; `stdio` dropped from one self-test child.
- e2e in a scratch copy: the preview build on port 4195 gave 3 skipped before and 3 passed after; the dev server on port 4196 skips all three with their reason. With a module that builds a schema at load and is imported before `src/env.ts`, the smoke specs' CSP guard gave 4 failed before and 4 passed after.
- Build: `dist/manifest.webmanifest` is the same before and after (15 keys); the `dist` file list is the same (41 files); `index.html` differs in one comment.
- `gate-integrity` in a scratch copy, for a fork that renames the app and changes its colours: before, `vite.config.ts` is listed as a gate change (exit 1); after, the edit lands in `app.config.ts` and no gate file is listed (exit 0).
- docs-check in a scratch clone with the sample code deleted: 6 findings, 1 in a gate file → 5 findings, 0 in gate files (the 5 are in the fork's own `.cursor/brain/*` docs).
- Contrast for every variant, at rest and on hover, in both themes: default on hover 4.13 → 5.94 (light) and 4.10 → 5.81 (dark); the other 18 pairs are unchanged, the lowest 4.85:1.

candidates.body:
Cells hold real memory addresses, so the VM has to turn numbers back into pointers throughout. Using indexes instead could remove most or all of the `unsafe` code, and turn several crashes into normal Forth errors.

This is a design proposal. None of it has been prototyped, so the effects below are expectations from reading the code.

## The problem

`Cell` is a `usize`, and Cells store addresses: word links, name pointers, threads, the `DOES>` action cell and code fields. Each use casts the number back to a pointer:

```rust
regs.w = *regs.ip as *const Cell;
```

Miri reports an integer-to-pointer cast at 7 places:

| File | Lines at `216ba73` | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `src/vm.rs` | `next`, `enter_word` | Reading threads and code fields |
| `src/dictionary.rs` | `find_word`, `is_execution_token` | Following links and names |
| `src/primitives/runtime.rs` | `dodoes`, `execute` | Action cells and execution tokens |

The code is allowed, but the pointer loses track of its allocation, so Miri warns that it might miss bugs. A passing Miri run therefore proves less than it seems to. Silencing the warning with `-Zmiri-permissive-provenance` wouldn't change that, and `with_exposed_provenance` gets the same warning.

The larger problem is that any Cell can be run as an address. That's behind the crashes in #15, #26 and #31, and it's why `outer_interpreter` has to be `unsafe`, as described in #14.

## Proposed design

- **Addresses become indexes** into the dictionary. Links, names, threads and action cells hold indexes, and all access is bounds-checked.
- **`ip` and `W` become indexes**, and the return stack holds indexes.
- **Code fields hold an index into a table of primitives**, in place of a function address. This removes the `transmute` in `enter_word`.
- **An out-of-range index is a `ForthError`**, in the inner interpreter as well as in `@` and `!`.

## Expected effects

- Most or all `unsafe` code goes away, including the `unsafe` on `boot` and `outer_interpreter`.
- The Miri warnings go away, and `-Zmiri-strict-provenance` can run.
- #15, #26 and #31 can no longer corrupt memory. Running a bad Cell would give an error, or wrong results in the VM, but not undefined behaviour.
- `!` can stay unrestricted, because overwriting a header can't reach outside the VM.
- The dictionary could grow, which it can't today because of raw addresses.
- Mutation testing would cover the primitives, because `cargo-mutants` skips `unsafe fn`.

This doesn't solve #32, because the stacks would still be unbounded.

## Open questions

- **Cell or byte addresses?** Cell indexes remove alignment errors, but `X 1 +` then means the next Cell, which differs from standard Forth addressing. Byte offsets keep that behaviour, but keep the alignment checks. #91 answers this: strings need to reach single bytes, so addresses stay in bytes. #92 relies on that for its `c-addr u` strings.
- **Where do names go?** They're bytes inside a Cell arena today. They could be packed into Cells, or kept in a separate byte buffer.
- **How does the trampoline work?** The text interpreter runs words through a thread in a local variable, which an index can't reach. It could use a reserved part of the dictionary.
- **How much slower is it?** Each step gains a bounds check. There are no measurements yet.
- **What happens to the fixes for #15, #26 and #31?** They'd no longer be needed for memory safety, but could still be wanted for better errors.

## Costs

This is a redesign of `vm.rs`, `dictionary.rs` and most primitives. Tests that assert on address arithmetic would need review. It's best decided before #15, #26 and #31 are fixed separately, because this could change or replace those fixes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The open questions have recorded decisions.
- Forth behaviour and the demo output stay the same, apart from intended changes to addresses.
- `boot` and `outer_interpreter` are safe functions, and any remaining `unsafe` is justified.
- Miri passes on both targets with `-Zmiri-strict-provenance`.
- The speed difference is measured and accepted.

candidates.body:
## Problem

Nothing keeps the GitHub Actions in the workflows up to date, so they drift apart: `ci.yml`, `lint.yml` and `mutants.yml` use `actions/checkout@v7`, while `claude.yml` and `claude-code-review.yml` still use `actions/checkout@v4`.

The project has no crate dependencies and no `rust-toolchain.toml`, so GitHub Actions is the only ecosystem with anything to update.

## Approach

Add `.github/dependabot.yml`, which GitHub runs itself. This adds no CI job, so the `Makefile` and the ruleset don't change.

- Only the `github-actions` ecosystem.
- A monthly schedule, because Actions are on major tags, and every update PR runs the full Miri jobs.
- All updates grouped into one PR, because the ruleset requires branches to be up to date with `main`, so separate PRs would keep making each other out of date.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` updates `github-actions` monthly, grouped into one PR.
- [ ] `claude-code-review.yml` skips its job on PRs opened by `dependabot[bot]`. Otherwise it fails on each of them, because `claude-code-action` refuses bots by default. This comes from reading the action's source, and hasn't been run.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` say that Dependabot PRs need no issue or changelog entry, and that the project owner reviews and merges them. Auto-merge stays off.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry.
- [ ] After the merge, Dependabot runs and opens a PR that moves `actions/checkout` in the two Claude workflows from `v4` to `v7`. This can only be checked after the merge, because Dependabot reads its configuration from `main`.

## Files

- `.github/dependabot.yml` (new)
- `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

## Out of scope

- The `cargo` ecosystem, until the project has dependencies.
- Pinning Actions to commit SHAs.
- Excluding Dependabot PRs from `make metrics`. From reading the code, they seem to count toward lead time. See #86.
- Turning on Dependabot alerts, which is a repository setting for the project owner. They are off now.

Closes #33

## Summary

Adds more checks to CI, and a `Makefile` to run the same steps locally. CI calls the `Makefile` targets, so the two can't drift apart.

| Check | Where it runs | Run time |
|---|---|---|
| Tests in release mode | `build-and-test`, every push | Seconds |
| Rustdoc, with warnings as errors | `build-and-test`, every push | Seconds |
| Tests under Miri, 64-bit | New `miri` job, every push | About 2 minutes |
| Tests under Miri, 32-bit (`i686`) | New `miri` job, every push | About 2 minutes |
| Mutation testing | New `mutants.yml`, weekly or on demand | About 2 minutes |

## Makefile

`make ci` runs everything that works on stable, `make ci-all` adds Miri, and `make mutants` runs mutation testing. Each step is also its own target. The tool-dependent targets stop with install instructions, and never install anything.

## Code changes

No Forth behaviour changes.

- `long_threads_do_not_grow_the_rust_stack` uses a shorter thread under Miri, so that it still runs.
- `cell_index` computes `offset` once. Its two subtractions gave a mutant that no test could tell apart, because `start` is always aligned.

## Results

- **Miri:** all 171 tests pass on 64-bit and 32-bit. The only warnings are the expected integer-to-pointer casts.
- **Mutation testing:** 60 caught, 3 unviable, none missed.
- **Miri detects real problems:** on a temporary branch, a test reproducing #31 made the job fail with `Undefined Behavior`. The same test crashed a normal Linux test run with `double free or corruption`. #31 has been updated with this evidence. The test isn't in this PR, because the bug is still open.
- **Step order:** `make miri-32` is skipped when `make miri` fails, as happened on the temporary branch.

## Limits

- `cargo-mutants` skips every `unsafe fn`, and there are 61 of those, including all primitives, `find_word` and `write_header`. So it only covers about the safe half of the code, and `AGENTS.md` says the manual check is still needed.
- Two `parse_name` mutants are excluded, because they make the tests hang. That counts as detected, but it would fail every weekly run.
- Miri only checks code that tests run, so it can't see #15 or #26 until they have regression tests.
- Nightly is floating, so a broken nightly can fail the `miri` job for unrelated reasons.

## Testing

`make ci` passes locally, and the demo output is identical to `main`. Nightly and `cargo-mutants` aren't installed locally, so those were only run on GitHub.

The mutation workflow was tested with a temporary `push` trigger on a temporary branch, which has been deleted. It can't be started by hand until it's on `main`.

Part of #125: step 3, "Show the development".

## What it does

- Each push to `main` appends its figures as one line to `history.jsonl` on the orphan branch `perf-data`. ## Summary
`@` and `!` are limited to the dictionary arena. Embedded hosts can now authorize already mapped register ranges, and Forth can register/revoke subranges, access individual registers, and copy blocks between MMIO and reserved dictionary buffers.

Adds `MMIO@`, `MMIO!`, `MMIO>DICT`, `DICT>MMIO`, `MMIO-REGISTER`, `MMIO-UNREGISTER` and composable rights/width flags. Block counts are bytes; the increment flag selects consecutive registers or a fixed FIFO address. All validation completes before the first device access. The host pointer is preserved for provenance; the unsafe `Vm::allow_mmio` contract covers mapping, lifetime, aliasing and synchronization. This does not include a bare-metal port or physical-memory mapping.

MMIO primitives, helpers, flag words, and their unit tests live in `src/primitives/mmio.rs`; `src/primitives/mod.rs` registers the words. Includes typed errors, public API coverage, a host-buffer demo, documentation and a gated performance workload.

Closes #179. Related to #14, #49, #130 and #172.

## Validation
- After the module extraction (`14860c5`), `make ci` and focused MMIO Miri checks on both 64-bit and 32-bit targets passed: 8 unit tests and 8 public API tests per target. Primitive bodies were moved verbatim.
- `make ci`: passed (formatting, both Clippy configurations, build, debug/release/minimal-feature tests and documentation).
- Full `make -j2 ci-all` on `4fd0eb4` ended without complete success summaries; do not treat the full Miri suite as passed. Local log: `/private/tmp/mmio-ci-all-final.log`.
- Deliberately weakened range validation and inverted FIFO stepping in an isolated copy: each mutation failed the expected tests with exit 101, using `--no-fail-fast`; production code remained intact.
- Incremental mutation testing after strengthening boundary, FIFO-span and both-byte-order tests: 134 mutants; 132 caught, 1 unviable, 1 equivalent survivor. The survivor replaces `MMIO_READ | MMIO_WRITE` with XOR; the constants are distinct single bits (1 and 2), so both expressions equal 3. The advisory command returns 2 for this equivalent mutant.
- `make demo-expected`: reviewed; only the MMIO section and menu renumbering changed.
- `make perf-pad-check`: MMIO workload passed (+0.14%, +0.06%). Overall check failed on the existing boot workload (+2.15%, +1.31% against a 1% absolute limit). Unmodified `origin/main` also failed on boot (-2.85%); other gated workloads passed. No unrelated benchmark policy changes are included.

## Hardware limitations
Tests use host-owned memory and a recording backend to verify access widths, addresses, order and count. Real device behavior, bus faults and required hardware barriers remain the embedding host's responsibility. Volatile is not atomic, and a hardware fault can leave a partial block transfer.

- **`.github/rulesets/protect-perf-data.json`** blocks deletion and force-pushes of `perf-data`, for everyone, admins included. It has no bypass.
- **`.github/rulesets/perf-data-writers.json`** refuses pushes, with two bypasses: the GitHub Actions app (id `15368`, from `gh api /apps/github-actions`), which the `record` job pushes with, and the repository admin role, for fixing the history by hand. The bypasses are in a separate ruleset because a bypass applies to every rule in its ruleset, and they must not allow deletion.
- **`.github/rulesets/protect-main.json`** now follows the live "Protect main" ruleset (id 26679927), which was changed on GitHub by hand. Compared field by field, after leaving out the fields GitHub sets itself. It adds:
  - an admin bypass in `pull_request` mode;

  - more PR parameters.

  One setting is stricter than GitHub on purpose: `allowed_merge_methods` is only `squash`, while GitHub still allows merge, squash and rebase.
- **`make protect`** applies every file in `.github/rulesets/`. It reads the name from each file, and updates the ruleset with that name or creates it. `RULESETS=<files>` limits it to some files. It now needs python3, to read the name.

The `perf-data` rulesets aren't active until an admin runs `make protect` after the merge. For `main`, applying it changes only the merge methods, to squash only.

candidates.body:
Cells no longer hold native pointers. The dictionary is a byte arena, and
every address is a byte offset into it, checked on every access, also in
the inner interpreter. An execution token is an index into an XT table in
Dictionary, whose entry holds the word's Code (primitive index, colon,
variable, constant, or DOES> action) and the address of its body. Headers
stay in the arena, with the XT in place of the code field.

NEXT fetches an XT and dispatches on its Code. The trampoline and the zero
end marker are gone: the text interpreter runs a word with NO_IP as its
return address. EXECUTE, COMPILE, and >BODY check an XT in constant time,
and LIT and EXIT have the fixed XTs 0 and 1. The word search stops at a
link that doesn't point back, so a header changed by ! can't make it loop.

The library and binary forbid unsafe code, so boot, outer_interpreter,
quit_loop and Vm::word_names are safe. ForthError::NullCodeField is gone.

Related to #49 and #39.

Closes #92

Adds `S"`, `."`, `ABORT"`, `COUNT`, `CR`, `SPACE`, `SPACES`, `CHAR`, `[CHAR]`, `CMOVE`, `CMOVE>` and `COMPARE`. `EMIT` and `TYPE` were already in #170.

**Design**

- Interpreted `S"` copies its text into one of two 256-byte transient buffers in the dictionary, below `HERE`. Two strings in a row are both valid, and a third reuses the first buffer. A longer text gives `StringTooLong`. The buffers take 512 bytes of every dictionary at boot.
- Compiled strings are `BRANCH` over the bytes, then two literals. The thread needs no inline operand, and an aborted definition rolls the bytes back.
- `."` and `ABORT"` compile calls to `TYPE` and the hidden `(ABORT")`. Their CFAs are captured at install time, so a user's `: TYPE ... ;` can't shadow them.
- `ABORT"` prints its text and then does `ABORT`, which the interpreter reports as `Abort`, with no message.
- `CMOVE` copies forward and `CMOVE>` copies backward. They differ from `MOVE` on overlapping ranges, and the tests check that.
- Strings hold bytes, so `CHAR` and `[CHAR]` give the first byte of a name.

**Errors:** `UnterminatedString` and `StringTooLong`, pinned in `errors_have_stable_messages`.

**Tests:** unit tests next to each primitive and in `dictionary.rs` and `input.rs`, API tests in `tests/forth.rs`, and a demo section with three error-section entries. I regenerated `tests/demo_output.txt` and checked that only the new lines changed. I also broke four behaviors on purpose, and each one fails a test.

**Checks:** `make ci` and `make ci-all` (MSRV and Miri) pass locally.

**Follow-up:** the byte-arena refactor is in #172. It's separate, because it touches the same `dictionary.rs` code.

Closes #138.

## Why

`claude-review` failed on #135 with `App token exchange failed: 401 Unauthorized - User does not have write access on this repository`. That run's actor is the `Copilot` bot. The action trades the run's OIDC token for a Claude app token, and Anthropic's server refuses actors without write access. `allowed_bots` alone doesn't help, because the action reads it only after that exchange.

## Change

In `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`:

- When `github.actor` is `Copilot`, pass `github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`, which makes the action skip the token exchange. Other actors get an empty string and keep the Claude app token as before.
- `allowed_bots: 'Copilot'`, so the action's human actor check lets that one bot through. Not `'*'`.
- `pull-requests: write`, so the review can post its comments with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. On bot runs those comments come from `github-actions[bot]`.

## Testing

- `make ci` passes, and the workflow file parses as YAML. No Rust code changed.
- I couldn't test the bot path from this PR, because its actor is the owner, so this run only shows that the normal path still works. The real check is the next run with `Copilot` as the actor, such as #135 after it's updated from `main`.
- The cause comes from the action's source (`src/github/token.ts`, `src/github/validation/actor.ts`) and the failed run's API data, not from a reproduction.

No `CHANGELOG.md` entry, because this only changes CI.

candidates.body:
In the standard, `QUIT` never returns. Here, `outer_interpreter` returns `Err(Quit)` or `Err(Abort)` to the host, so every library user has to write the loop that `QUIT` stands for. `forth-vm` had its own copy of that loop in `interactive`.

- **`quit_loop` (`src/interpreter.rs`, exported from `lib.rs`)**
  - It reads lines through a closure that gets the `&Vm`, which `rustyline` Tab completion needs.
  - It evaluates each line and reports a `LineResult` (`Ok`, `Quit`, `Abort` or `Error(ForthError)`) through a second closure. The library prints nothing.
  - `QUIT`, `ABORT` and errors end only their own line, and `ABORT` still clears the data stack.
  - It returns `Some(code)` when `BYE` runs and `None` at the end of the input, so a host only sees those two endings.
- **`outer_interpreter`**
  - It is unchanged: it still evaluates one piece of text and returns `ForthError::Quit` or `Abort`. Its docs and the `ForthError` docs now say so and point to `quit_loop`.
- **`forth-vm` (`src/main.rs`)**
  - `interactive` now uses `quit_loop`, for both the terminal and piped input.
  - The demo path still calls `outer_interpreter`, so `tests/demo_output.txt` doesn't change.
- **Tests and docs**
  - New API tests in `tests/forth.rs`:
    - `QUIT` keeps the data stack, and `ABORT` clears it, each at the top level and from a colon word.
    - An error ends only its own line.
    - `BYE` ends the loop with its code.
    - The end of the input ends the loop.
  - A doc example, a README note on `QUIT`, and a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `### Added`.

```rust
let bye = quit_loop(
    &mut vm,
    |_| lines.next(),
    |vm, result| match result {
        LineResult::Ok if !vm.is_compiling() => println!("ok"),
        LineResult::Error(e) => println!("Forth Error: {e}"),
        _ => {}
    },
);
```

Design choices for review: the loop is a new function rather than a change to `outer_interpreter`, so existing callers are unaffected. Lines come from a closure instead of a `BufRead`, because `rustyline` doesn't fit a `BufRead`. Results go to a closure, so the host decides what to print. Not done here: sharing one input buffer with `KEY` and `ACCEPT` (see #122).

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #103

Closes #26. Third of the "Before" items in #114, and needed by #15 (`COMPILE,`).

## Changes

- New flag `F_COMPILE_ONLY` (`1 << 12`) and accessor `is_compile_only` in `src/dictionary.rs`.
- `is_execution_token` refuses a word with this flag, so `EXECUTE` and `>BODY` give `InvalidExecutionToken`. No new error is needed.
- `LIT` gets `F_HIDDEN | F_COMPILE_ONLY`. The comment there says that every word with an inline operand, such as the branch words in #119, needs the flag.
- README and `CHANGELOG.md` say what is refused and why.

## Tests

- Unit tests: the flag bit, `is_execution_token` with the flag (also after `finish_last`), and `EXECUTE` on `LIT` leaving the stack and `IP` alone.
- API tests in `tests/forth.rs` for both cases of #26, from the text interpreter and from a colon word, plus `>BODY`. Each one checks that the VM still works after the error.

## Checks

- Before: on `main` case 2 aborts with a misaligned pointer panic. After: both cases give `Invalid execution token` in debug and release builds, run with the `forth-vm` binary.
- `make ci` passes, and `tests/demo_output.txt` is unchanged. There is no demo block, because `LIT` is hidden.
- Mutation checks: removing the check in `is_execution_token` fails a test, and removing the flag from `LIT` aborts the test binaries, as in the bug.
